newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Reform headed for official opposition.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Reform headed for official opposition.

text.p: Canada's right-wing Reform party was set to become the official opposition in Parliament, displacing the separatist Bloc Quebecois, the French CBC and the Canadian Press news agency said on Monday.
Reform was ahead or elected in 50 of 301 seats so far, with the Bloc Quebecois leading or having won in 44 seats, television stations reported.
The ruling Liberals were ahead or had won in 156 ridings, according to television stations -- enough to form a majority in the 301-seat House of Commons.
Most Liberal support came from Ontario, while Reform surged ahead in the Western provinces of Alberta and British Columbia.
Reform advocates smaller government, tax cuts, tough measures against crime and a no-nonsense approach to Quebec's secessionist aspirations.
Support for the New Democrats was strong in Saskatchewan and the Atlantic provinces, and the Conservatives made breakthroughs in Atlantic Canada.
